due_when.clears_when: A MECHANISM refuses the push, not a resolver that promises to be careful. The cheapest honest one: a pre-push or CI check that greps every tracked text file in the diff for a conflict marker at line start and fails. [!] A CAREFUL RESOLVER DOES NOT CLEAR THIS, and that is the whole finding - the resolver that did this ALREADY printed that it could not handle the file. The defect was not ignorance, it was proceeding anyway. [!] NOR DOES 'the manager will stop batch-resolving': this repo's own record on `reminder is not a mechanism` (MI-15, twice) is why that is not accepted as a disposition.

origin.ref: session_01XQhayAHWdrSYv8jN54P2HH (manager), commit 983eb7a2 (dropped in E5's rebuild), PR #12739
origin.rerun: git log --all -S'<<<<<<<' --oneline -- scripts/ | head   # any commit that ADDED a conflict marker to a tracked file is an instance of this class; the 2026-09-22 one is gone from history (rebuilt away), so an empty result is NOT evidence the hazard is fixed - read the clears_when

routed_to: unrouted -- needs a lane; small and self-contained
what: A MANAGER PUSHED scripts/ci/run_guards.py WITH CONFLICT MARKERS IN IT to a live lane branch on 2026-09-22, and the mechanism is the finding rather than the incident. The batch resolver handled PIPELINE.jsonl and MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json by name, PRINTED 'UNHANDLED' for run_guards.py on stdout, and then ran `git add` over EVERY conflicted path regardless - so it correctly identified that it could not resolve the file, said so, and pushed it anyway. [!] A LOOP THAT REPORTS A PROBLEM AND THEN PROCEEDS IS WORSE THAN ONE THAT NEVER CHECKED: it leaves a record saying it looked. That is the same shape as the `unprovenanced diagnostic output` class this repo already has a guard for, and the same shape as `new-table-wiring-guard`'s presence-only marker - a check whose output nothing acts on. [!] THE BLAST RADIUS WAS THE WHOLE GUARD FLEET: run_guards.py is the module every guard run imports, so on that branch it did not parse and the entire required `guards` context could not run - INCLUDING check_manager_scope.py, the guard that grades the manager. A manager error disabled the guard that watches the manager. It was caught in ~90 seconds by the next CI run and repaired, and the repair itself then graded as a manager-scope violation, which cost a branch rebuild by the E5 lane to clear. [!] THE ORIGINAL COMMIT IS GONE FROM HISTORY - E5 rebuilt the branch from main without it, so `git log -S'<<<<<<<'` finds nothing today. An empty probe is therefore NOT evidence of absence here; it is evidence the incident was cleaned up. The rerun command says so.
